columns.name: ofds_id
columns.title: Identifier
columns.description: A universally unique identifier for this network, as defined by [RFC 4122](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4122). For more information, see the [identifier reference](https://open-fibre-data-standard.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/identifiers.html).

columns.name: name
columns.title: Network name
columns.description: A name for this network.

columns.name: website
columns.title: Website
columns.description: The URL of the website for this network.

columns.name: publisher__name
columns.title: Publisher Name
columns.description: The publisher of this network. A name for this organisation.

columns.name: publisher__identifier__id
columns.title: Publisher Organisation identifier Identifier
columns.description: The publisher of this network. An identifier for this organisation. The identifier assigned to the organisation in the register identified in `.scheme`.

columns.name: publisher__identifier__scheme
columns.title: Publisher Organisation identifier Scheme
columns.description: The publisher of this network. An identifier for this organisation. The register from which the identifier in `.id` is drawn, from the open [organisationIdentifierScheme codelist](https://open-fibre-data-standard.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/codelists.html#organisationidentifierscheme).

columns.name: publisher__identifier__legalName
columns.title: Publisher Organisation identifier Legal name
columns.description: The publisher of this network. An identifier for this organisation. The legally registered name of the organisation

columns.name: publisher__identifier__uri
columns.title: Publisher Organisation identifier URI
columns.description: The publisher of this network. An identifier for this organisation. A canonical URI for this identifier, such as those provided by Open Corporates. Do not use this field to provide the website of the organisation: instead, use `Organisation.website`.

columns.name: publicationDate
columns.title: Publication date
columns.description: The date when this network was published.

columns.name: collectionDate
columns.title: Collection date
columns.description: The date when the location data was collected. If a dataset was produced by digitising a map, the date that the data for the map was collected.

columns.name: accuracy
columns.title: Accuracy
columns.description: The horizontal uncertainty, in metres, of the coordinates in this dataset relative to the datum of the coordinate reference system specified in `crs`. Further details about the accuracy of coordinates in this dataset can be provided in `.accuracyDetails`.

columns.name: accuracyDetails
columns.title: Accuracy details
columns.description: Further details about the accuracy specified in `accuracy`. For example, the confidence level of the accuracy measurement, the methodology used to calculate the accuracy, or a local classification of accuracy.

columns.name: language
columns.title: Language
columns.description: The default language of this network,from the open [language codelist](https://open-fibre-data-standard.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/codelists.html#language). A [BCP47 language tag](https://www.w3.org/International/articles/language-tags/) is allowed, if there is a user need for the additional information.

columns.name: ofds_id
columns.title: Identifier
columns.description: An identifier for this node. The identifier must be unique within the scope of the `nodes` array.

columns.name: name
columns.title: Node name
columns.description: A name for this node.

columns.name: phase
columns.title: Phase
columns.description: The phase to which this node belongs.

columns.name: status
columns.title: Status
columns.description: The status of this node, from the closed [nodeStatus codelist](https://open-fibre-data-standard.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/codelists.html#nodestatus).

columns.name: address__streetAddress
columns.title: Node address Street address
columns.description: The physical address of this node. The street address. For example, 1600 Amphitheatre Pkwy.

columns.name: address__locality
columns.title: Node address Locality
columns.description: The physical address of this node. The locality. For example, Mountain View.

columns.name: address__region
columns.title: Node address Region
columns.description: The physical address of this node. The region. For example, CA.

columns.name: address__postalCode
columns.title: Node address Postal code
columns.description: The physical address of this node. The postal code. For example, 94043.

columns.name: address__country
columns.title: Node address Country
columns.description: The physical address of this node. The country in which the address is physically located, from the closed [country codelist](https://open-fibre-data-standard.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/codelists.html#country).

columns.name: accessPoint
columns.title: Access point
columns.description: Whether active or passive transmission equipment is installed at this node which is capable of providing access to the network.

columns.name: power
columns.title: Power availability
columns.description: Whether power for active network equipment is available at this node.

columns.name: physicalInfrastructureProvider
columns.title: Physical infrastructure provider
columns.description: The organisation that owns the passive network infrastructure for this node, i.e. the non-electrical elements, such as dark fibre, ducts and physical sites.

columns.name: ofds_id
columns.title: Identifier
columns.description: An identifier for this span. The identifier must be unique within the scope of the `spans` array.

columns.name: name
columns.title: Span name
columns.description: A name for this span.

columns.name: phase
columns.title: Phase
columns.description: The phase to which this span belongs.

columns.name: status
columns.title: Span status
columns.description: The status of the network infrastructure for this span, from the closed [spanStatus codelist](https://open-fibre-data-standard.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/codelists.html#spanstatus).

columns.name: readyForServiceDate
columns.title: Ready for service date
columns.description: The date this span was ready to carry traffic. For spans with multiple network providers, the earliest of the dates at which each provider's network was ready to carry traffic on this span.

columns.name: start
columns.title: Start
columns.description: The identifier of one of two nodes that this span connects. It must match the `.id` of a node in the `nodes` array. If `directed == true`, it represents the starting point of the span. Otherwise, the distinction between `start` and `end` is arbitrary.

columns.name: end
columns.title: End
columns.description: The identifier of one of two nodes that this span connects. It must match the `.id` of a node in the `nodes` array. If `directed == true`, it represents the end point of the span. Otherwise, the distinction between `start` and `end` is arbitrary.

columns.name: directed
columns.title: Directed
columns.description: Whether this span is directed. If `True`, then `.start` represents the start of the span and `.end` represents the end. Otherwise, `.start` and `.end` reference this span's endpoints with no direction implied.

columns.name: physicalInfrastructureProvider
columns.title: Physical infrastructure provider
columns.description: The organisation that owns the passive network infrastructure for this span, i.e. the non-electrical elements, such as dark fibre, ducts and physical sites.

columns.name: supplier
columns.title: Supplier
columns.description: The organisation responsible for installing the cable for this span.

columns.name: deploymentDetails__description
columns.title: Deployment details Description
columns.description: Further details of this span's deployment. A description of this span's deployment.

columns.name: darkFibre
columns.title: Dark fibre availability
columns.description: Whether access to dark fibre is available on this span.

columns.name: fibreType
columns.title: Fibre type
columns.description: The type of fibre used in this span, from the closed [fibreType codelist](https://open-fibre-data-standard.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/codelists.html#fibretype). Further details of the span's fibre type can be provided in `.fibreTypeDetails`.

columns.name: fibreTypeDetails__fibreSubtype
columns.title: Fibre type details Fibre subtype
columns.description: Further details about this span's fibre type. The sub-category of the fibre type. For example, G.652.B.

columns.name: fibreTypeDetails__description
columns.title: Fibre type details Description
columns.description: Further details about this span's fibre type. A description of this span's fibre type.

columns.name: fibreCount
columns.title: Fibre count
columns.description: The number of individual optical fibres in this span.

columns.name: fibreLength
columns.title: Fibre length
columns.description: The physical length in kilometres, of fibre optic cable used in this span.

columns.name: capacity
columns.title: Capacity
columns.description: The transmission rate, or throughput, of this span, expressed in Gbit/sec (Gbps). The equipped capacity is the total capacity of the circuits (e.g. E1, DS3, STM-1 etc.) which have been activated in the network transmission equipment of the span. For spans with multiple network providers, the sum of the capacity of each provider's network on this span. Further details of this span's capacity can be provided in `.capacityDetails`.

columns.name: capacityDetails__description
columns.title: Capacity details Description
columns.description: Further details about this span's capacity A description of this span's capacity.

contractType.csv: Public Private Partnership (PPP): A long-term contract between a private party and a government entity,for providing a public asset or service,in which the private party bears significant risk and management responsibility and remuneration is linked to performance.
Private: A contract in which the private sector takes ownership of the network and responsibility for its operation.
Public: A contract in which the public sector owns the network and is responsible for its operation.
nodeType.csv: Add drop site: A point at which individual digital bit streams can be added to, or dropped from, a multiplexed signal in order to redirect bit streams between network paths.
Aggregation point: A point at which multiple fibre optic cables are spliced together. Typically located between an exchange or POP and GPON splitters or end user premises.

Border crossing: The point at which a fibre cable crosses either an international boundary or the coastline of the operator’s country. The countries to which this node connects should be listed in `.internationalConnections`.
Cabinet: An distribution cabinet to which end users are connected by a standard phone line.
Cable landing point: The location where a submarine or other underwater cable makes landfall.
Data centre: A structure, or group of structures, dedicated to the centralized accommodation, interconnection and operation of information technology and network telecommunications equipment.
Internet Exchange Point: A physical point at which networks such as internet service providers, mobile operators and content delivery networks come together to connect and exchange internet traffic.
Point of Presence: A demarcation point, access point, or physical location at which two or more networks or communication devices share a connection.
Repeater site: A point at which fibre optic signals are amplified or repeated. Also known as a regeneration facility.
Tower: A ground-based or rooftop structure that supports antennas for sending or receiving radio waves.
nodeTechnologies.csv: Internet Protocol: A network layer protocol that defines the addressing mechanism on the Internet to allow data to be transmitted.
Multi-Protocol Label Switching: A routing technique that directs data from one node to the next based on labels rather than network addresses.
spanTechnologies.csv: Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing: A technology that multiplexes a number of optical carrier signals onto a single optical fibre by using different wavelengths.
Synchronous Digital Hierarchy: A standardised protocol for transferring multiple digital bit streams synchronously over optical fibre. SDH is used worldwide, with the exception of the US and Canada.
Synchronous Optical Networking: A standardised protocol for transferring multiple digital bit streams synchronously over optical fibre. SONET is used in the US and Canada.
Time Division Multiplexing: A technology that multiplexes a number of optical carrier signals onto a single optical fibre by using different arrival times.
organisationRole.csv: Physical infrastructure provider: An organisation that owns and maintains passive network infrastructure, i.e. the non-electrical elements, such as dark fibre, ducts and physical sites.

Network provider: An organisation that operates the active network infrastructure, i.e. the electrical elements, such as optical transceivers, switches and routers. In open business models, network providers provide wholesale access to service providers such as retail internet service providers. Network providers can own or lease the active network infrastructure.
Funder: An organisation that provides financing for the development or operation of a phase or network.
Supplier: The organisation responsible for installing the cable for a span.

nodeStatus.csv: Proposed: Planning for the node is at an early stage and financing for its construction is not yet finalised.
Planned: Planning for the node is at an advanced stage and financing for its construction is finalised.
Under construction: Construction of the passive physical infrastructure for the node is in progress.
Inactive: Construction of the passive network infrastructure is complete, but the node is not yet operational.
Operational: The active network infrastructure for at least one network provider at the node is live and carrying traffic.
Decommissioned: The node is no longer operational.

fibreType.csv: G.651.1: A 50/125 µm multimode graded index optical fibre cable for the optical access network that conforms to ITU-T recommendation G.651.1.
G.652: A single-mode optical fibre and cable that conforms to ITU-T recommendation G.652.
G.653: A dispersion-shifted, single-mode optical fibre and cable that conforms to ITU-T recommendation G.653.
G.654: A cut-off shifted single-mode optical fibre and cable that conforms to ITU-T recommendation G.654.
G.655: A non-zero dispersion-shifted single-mode optical fibre and cable that conforms to ITU-T recommendation G.655.
G.656: A fibre and cable with non-zero dispersion for wideband optical transport that conforms to ITU-T recommendation G.656.
G.657: A bending-loss insensitive single-mode optical fibre and cable that conforms to ITU-T recommendation G.657.

transmissionMedium.csv: Coaxial cable: The physical media of this span is coaxial cable.
Copper wire: The physical media of this span is copper wire.
Fibre optic cable: The physical media of this span is fibre optic cable.
Microwave radio: The physical media of this span is microwave radio.
deployment.csv: Above ground: This span is deployed above ground. For example, aerial deployment along poles or using optical groundwire.
Below ground: This span is deployed below ground. For example, cable that is routed through a duct buried in a trench or run through a sewer.
